title: Which processor is this?
prompt:
Mira documents the machine she works on. The kernel describes the processor in `/proc/cpuinfo`.

Save the line that gives the processor’s model name (it starts with `model name`) into `cpu.txt` in her home directory, exactly as `/proc/cpuinfo` shows it.
hints: `/proc/cpuinfo` is a text file the kernel makes up when it is read: `less /proc/cpuinfo` shows it.
`grep` picks out the lines that contain a text.
check:
if [ ! -e cpu.txt ]; then no "There is no cpu.txt yet. Create it in Mira’s home directory."; exit 1; fi
ok "cpu.txt exists."
want=$(grep -m 1 'model name' /proc/cpuinfo)
if [ "$(head -n 1 cpu.txt)" = "$want" ]; then ok "It holds the model name line: $(printf '%s' "$want" | tr -s '\t ' ' ')"
else no "It doesn’t start with the model name line of /proc/cpuinfo."; fi

title: A megabyte of zeros
prompt:
To test a disk tool, Ada needs an empty disk image: a file `blank.img` in Mira’s home directory that holds exactly 1 MiB (1048576 bytes), all of them zero bytes.

Make it from the device file that produces zero bytes.
hints: `/dev/zero` is a virtual device: reading it gives an endless stream of zero bytes.
`head -c 1M` stops after 1 MiB. `dd` can do it too: `bs` is the block size and `count` the number of blocks.
`head -c 1M /dev/zero > blank.img`, or `dd if=/dev/zero of=blank.img bs=1024 count=1024`.
check:
if [ ! -e blank.img ]; then no "There is no blank.img yet. Create it in Mira’s home directory."; exit 1; fi
ok "blank.img exists."
size=$(stat -c %s blank.img)
if [ "$size" = 1048576 ]; then ok "It is exactly 1048576 bytes."; else no "It is $size bytes, not 1048576."; fi
if [ "$size" -gt 0 ] && cmp -s -n "$size" blank.img /dev/zero; then ok "Every byte is zero."; else no "Not all of its bytes are zero bytes."; fi
